title: Birational comparison on the codimension induction bad locus
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite field $B$ of characteristic $\ell$, and an integer $c\geq1$. For a Noetherian scheme $Z$, write $\operatorname{ht}_Z(z)=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ and say that a closed subset has codimension at least $a$ when every point in it has height at least $a$; the empty closed subset has every codimension. Assume the following induction hypothesis: for every Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $Z$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, every open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow Z$, and every $L\in D^b_c(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, there is a closed subset $C\subseteq Z$ of codimension at least $c$ such that $(Rv_*L)|_{Z\setminus C}$ is bounded constructible. Let $X$ be integral Noetherian quasi-excellent with $\ell$ invertible, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a dense open immersion, let $K\in D^b_c(U_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, and let $T\subseteq X$ be an integral reduced closed subscheme with generic point $t$ of height $c$, such that $Rj_*K$ is bounded constructible on $X\setminus T$. Let $p:X'\to X$ be a proper morphism of integral schemes, an isomorphism over some dense open of $X$, and let $(e_i:E_i\to X')$ be a finite completely decomposed family of separated finite-type etale morphisms (every point of $X'$ lifts with the same residue field). Put $U'=U\times_XX'$, let $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ be its inclusion, and set $K'=p_U^*K$. After restricting $X$ to some open neighbourhood of $t$ and base changing all these data, there is a reduced closed subscheme $T'=\coprod_{\alpha}T'_\alpha\subseteq X'$, a finite disjoint union of integral subschemes, each finite and surjective over $T$, such that $Rj'_*K'$ is bounded constructible on $X'\setminus T'$. For every $\alpha$, some $e_{i_\alpha}$ has a section $s_\alpha:T'_\alpha\to E_{i_\alpha}$ over $X'$. If $i:T\hookrightarrow X$ and $i':T'\hookrightarrow X'$ are the inclusions and $p_T:T'\to T$ is induced by $p$, the composite of the base-change unit and restriction,
$$i^*Rj_*K\longrightarrow R(p_T)_*i'^*Rj'_*K',$$
has a cone in $D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. The finite family of components of $T'$ is allowed to be empty. The scheme and coefficient notions are [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; local ring dimension means Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: XIII 3.2.2, Proposition 3.4.2 and 3.5.1 (including generic sections of the completely decomposed cover)

proof.text: We work throughout on ordinary small etale sites with constant coefficients $B$. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and constructible pullback [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback] show that pullback preserves $D^b_c$: cohomology commutes with the exact functor, and its cohomological interval is unchanged. For the finite field $B$, the underlying sets of finite modules are finite, so the set-sheaf constructibility criterion is equivalent to the module criterion. The long exact cohomology sequence and [thm-constructible-serre] show that $D^b_c$ is closed under shifts and distinguished triangles; retracts are handled by the same kernel/image criterion. Derived direct image carries triangles to triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. A finite map has exact direct image on abelian sheaves by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]; [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] gives exactness and vanishing also for $B$-module direct images. Extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Thus the open-closed short exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], applied to complexes, gives its usual distinguished triangle, with underived closed direct image.

Because $p$ is proper, it is finite type and quasi-compact. The stability statement [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] makes $X'$, its open subschemes and its closed subschemes Noetherian quasi-excellent; the same applies to closed subschemes and opens of $X$. The prime $\ell$ stays invertible under these restrictions and base changes. Step 1 gives $K'=p_U^*K\in D^b_c(U',B)$. Apply the assumed induction hypothesis, with its same integer $c$, to $(X',j',K')$, obtaining a reduced closed subset $C\subset X'$ all of whose points have height at least $c$, with $M:=Rj'_*K'$ bounded constructible on $X'\setminus C$. Open restriction of all direct images and units is valid by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization].

source.place: XIII 3.2.2, application of the induction hypothesis on X prime

proof.text: Let $D$ be an irreducible component of $C$, with generic point $y$, and put $s=p(y)$. Properness makes $p(D)=\overline{\{s\}}$ closed. Since $p$ is an isomorphism over a dense open, its map on function fields is an isomorphism. The inequality of [lem-trf-local-dimension-formula], applied to $p$ at $y$, therefore gives $\operatorname{ht}_{X'}(y)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y)\leq\operatorname{ht}_X(s)$. If $t\in p(D)$, then $s$ generalizes $t$, so $\operatorname{ht}_X(s)\leq c$. Together with $\operatorname{ht}_{X'}(y)\geq c$ this forces equality throughout and $s=t$: a strict specialization increases height by at least one, by appending a prime to a chain. It also forces $\kappa(y)/\kappa(t)$ algebraic. Remove the finitely many closed sets $p(D)$ for components not meeting the fibre over $t$. Every remaining component consequently maps onto $T$; the factorization through its reduced scheme structure follows on affine charts because an equation vanishing at every point of a reduced scheme is zero.

source.place: XIII 3.2.2, height inequality and removal of the other components

proof.text: For each remaining integral component $D\to T$, the generic fibre is integral with algebraic function field over $\kappa(t)$. Each nonempty affine chart of that fibre has coordinate domain a finitely generated $\kappa(t)$-subalgebra of this algebraic field. Finitely many algebraic generators span a finite-dimensional algebra (bound each exponent by a polynomial relation), and a finite-dimensional domain over a field is a field: multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective, hence surjective, linear endomorphism. Each such chart therefore consists of one point. Irreducibility makes these the same point, so the generic fibre has one point. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] to each $D\to T$; these maps are finite type, quasi-compact and separated, and $T$ is Noetherian. After shrinking $T$ about $t$, all are finite surjective. This is achieved by an open restriction of $X$, since every open of $T$ is induced from $X$. Distinct components have distinct generic points over $t$, so their intersections have closed proper images in $T$. Remove those images as well. With reduced structures the surviving closed set is now $T'=\coprod_\alpha T'_\alpha$, a disjoint union of integral schemes finite surjective over $T$. The complement of $T'$ is the good complement of the restricted $C$ from Step 2. The construction also works when no component survives.

source.place: XIII 3.2.2, finite and disjoint bad components

proof.text: For the generic point $y_\alpha$ of each $T'_\alpha$, complete decomposition gives an $i_\alpha$ and a $\kappa(y_\alpha)$-point of $E_{i_\alpha}$ above it, hence a section of $E_{i_\alpha}\times_{X'}T'_\alpha$ at that generic point. The affine open neighbourhoods of $y_\alpha$ form a small cofiltered system of qcqs schemes with affine transitions whose limit is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T'_\alpha,y_\alpha}=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y_\alpha)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods]. Its etale target is locally finitely presented. Thus [lem-sbc-pointed-section-stage-descent] extends the section to some open neighbourhood $V_\alpha$ of $y_\alpha$ in $T'_\alpha$, still over $T'_\alpha$. The closed set $T'_\alpha\setminus V_\alpha$ has closed image under its finite map to $T$, missing $t$. Remove these finitely many images by an open restriction of $X$. The sections are then defined on every surviving $T'_\alpha$. All previous properties persist under this restriction.

source.place: XIII 3.5.1 and II Proposition 2.2.3, extension of the generic sections

proof.text: Choose a dense open $W\subset U$ over which $p$ is an isomorphism, and let $a:Z=U\setminus W\hookrightarrow U$ be the reduced closed inclusion. The proper-finiteness statement [lem-per-proper-finite-coefficient-bounded-preservation] applies to the proper base change $p_U:U'\to U$, with the Noetherian schemes of Step 2. Both $K$ and $Rp_{U*}p_U^*K$ are bounded constructible. Complete the unit to a triangle $K\to Rp_{U*}p_U^*K\to C_U\to K[1]$. Step 1 gives $C_U\in D^b_c(U,B)$. By open localization its restriction to $W$ is zero: there the unit is the unit of an isomorphism. Apply the open-closed triangle of Step 1 to $C_U$. Its open-extension term is zero, so $C_U\simeq a_*H$ for $H=a^*C_U\in D^b_c(Z,B)$.

source.place: XIII Proposition 3.4.2, construction of the proper-unit defect on Z

proof.text: Let $\bar Z$ be the reduced closure of $Z$ in $X$, $b:\bar Z\hookrightarrow X$ its closed inclusion and $v:Z\hookrightarrow\bar Z$ the open inclusion. Since $W$ is dense in the integral scheme $X$, every component of $\bar Z$ has positive height in $X$. Apply the induction hypothesis on the Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $\bar Z$ to $(v,H)$. It gives a closed $A\subset\bar Z$ with every point of height at least $c$ in $\bar Z$, such that $Rv_*H$ is bounded constructible off $A$. Every point of $A$ has height at least $c+1$ in $X$: a chain of length $c$ in $\bar Z$ can be prefixed by the generic point of $X$, which is outside $\bar Z$. In particular $t\notin A$. As $A$ is closed in $X$, remove $A$ from $X$. After this restriction $Rv_*H$ is bounded constructible on all of $\bar Z$. Since $b$ is proper, [lem-per-proper-finite-coefficient-bounded-preservation] gives $Rb_*Rv_*H\in D^b_c(X,B)$. The canonical composition isomorphisms of [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] identify $Rj_*a_*H=Rb_*Rv_*H$, since $ja=bv$ and closed direct image is exact (Step 1). Thus $i^*Rj_*a_*H\in D^b_c(T,B)$. The case $Z=\varnothing$ has $H=0$ and needs no induction.

source.place: XIII Proposition 3.4.2, first stage: induction on the nowhere dense defect support

proof.text: Apply $i^*Rj_*$ to the triangle in Step 6. The last term is bounded constructible by Step 7. Write $F=X'\times_XT$, $k:F\hookrightarrow X'$ and $q:F\to T$. Derived direct-image composition [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] identifies the middle term before restriction with $Rp_*M$. Proper base change [det-properbasechange-modules] for $p$ identifies its restriction with $Rq_*k^*M$. This is applicable in $D^+$ because $M$ is bounded below, and every cohomology sheaf is killed by $\ell$. It follows that the canonical map $i^*Rj_*K\to Rq_*k^*M$ has bounded constructible cone. This is the first part of the specified comparison: if $\varepsilon_j$ is the counit for $j^*\dashv Rj_*$, the transpose under $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ of $Rj_*\eta_{p_U,K}$, using the composition isomorphisms, is the exchange $p^*Rj_*K\to Rj'_*p_U^*K$. Indeed transposing once more under $j'{}^*\dashv Rj'_*$ gives $p_U^*\varepsilon_{j,K}$; the other factors cancel by the two adjunction triangle identities. Transposing for $q$ after restricting gives exactly the proper base-change map followed by that unit.

source.place: XIII Proposition 3.4.2, first comparison and its canonical unit

proof.text: Let $d:T'\hookrightarrow F$ be the closed inclusion and $h:F\setminus T'\hookrightarrow F$ its complementary open. Put $L=k^*M$. Its restriction to $F\setminus T'$ is bounded constructible, because $M$ is so on $X'\setminus T'$ and pullback preserves this property (Steps 1--4). The open-closed triangle of Step 1 gives $h_!h^*L\to L\to d_*d^*L\to h_!h^*L[1]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], cohomology of the first term is extension by zero of that of $h^*L$. Adding the complementary closed stratum with zero module to each finite stratification proves constructibility, with the same bounded interval. Therefore $h_!h^*L\in D^b_c(F,B)$. Apply the proper-finiteness input [lem-per-proper-finite-coefficient-bounded-preservation] to $q$. Its direct image of the first term is bounded constructible, so $Rq_*L\to R(qd)_*d^*L$ has bounded constructible cone. The target is $R(p_T)_*i'{}^*M$ by direct-image composition, and the map is the direct image of the restriction unit. This argument permits $T'=\varnothing$, in which case $d_*d^*L=0$.

source.place: XIII Proposition 3.4.2, second stage: remove the good part of the proper fibre

proof.text: The arrow of the statement is the composite of the two arrows of Steps 8 and 9, with their stated adjunction units and restriction. The octahedral axiom of [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives a distinguished triangle from the cone of the first arrow to a cone of the composite to the cone of the second arrow. Both outer terms are in $D^b_c(T,B)$; closure under distinguished triangles, proved in Step 1 from [thm-constructible-serre], places the middle term there too. The finite surjectivity, disjointness, reduced structures and sections were obtained in Steps 4 and 5. Only finitely many open restrictions have been made, each containing $t$, so their intersection is the required open neighbourhood.

source.place: XIII Proposition 3.4.2 and 3.5.1, composition of the two comparisons

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q21-a97ccdbf6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its statement is unchanged from the Q23 import. I checked all ten steps against ILO XIII 3.2.2, 3.3, Prop 3.4.2 (both stages) and 3.5.1 in the local PDF. The route is the same: induction hypothesis on X'; the height argument through the 02JU dimension inequality (dominant, birational, so trdeg 0, giving s=t and kappa(y)/kappa(t) algebraic); one-point generic fibres, then 02NW makes the components finite surjective, and intersections miss t because the fibres over t are distinct points; generic sections spread by the affine-neighbourhood limit plus lfp section descent; the proper-unit triangle C ≅ a_*H; the induction hypothesis on Zbar, where prefixing (0) gives height ≥ c+1 so t is not in A; proper base change for M in D^+ with ell-torsion cohomology; the h_! triangle on F with q proper; the octahedral axiom. Every cited statement says what its step takes from it. I checked the edge cases: K=0, p an isomorphism, no surviving component, T'=∅, Z=∅, c=1. The new node lem-per-proper-finite-coefficient-bounded-preservation is statement-only and self-contained. It is true: Stacks 0GL0 (theorem-constructible-shriek) with the identity compactification, plus 095U (lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper) with a uniform fibre-dimension bound from finitely many charts; no finite dimension or invertibility is needed. It matches ILO's proper finiteness input and is not a clause of the item. On duplicates: lem-per-quasi-excellent-etale-direct-image-finiteness contains the proper case, but its closure reaches this item, so citing it would make a cycle. The pbc proper-finiteness nodes need finite dimension and invertibility, and the fd node needs a base over a field. Advisory: a later split of the new node can cite lem-weil-pbc-etale-compactification-constructibility and lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound; neither reaches the item. Batch 5: the closure from both targets, stopping at the assumption leaves, grows by only the new node. All three flagged citations are already in the closure without this item and are generic: det-properbasechange-modules is general proper base change, given by neither assumption; lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability is Stacks 07QU algebra, reaching lem-trf-g-ring-affine-cover only through G-ring algebra; lem-trf-local-dimension-formula is the 02JU inequality. All three are accepted. I accept all 16 tool_uses as generic inputs. There is no SGA citation. I made no changes.
